paras.en: So I lived alone, with no one I could really talk to, until an engine breakdown in the Sahara Desert six years ago. Something in my engine had broken. And since I had neither a mechanic nor any passengers with me, I got ready to attempt a difficult repair all by myself. For me, it was a matter of life or death. I had barely enough drinking water for eight days.
paras.zh: 我就这样独自生活，没有一个人能真正说说话，直到六年前，我在撒哈拉沙漠遇上了一次故障。我的发动机里有个部件坏了。身边既没有机械师，也没有乘客，我便准备试着独自完成这项艰难的修理。对我来说，这是生死攸关的事。我的饮用水勉强够喝八天。

paras.en: So on the first evening I fell asleep on the sand, a thousand miles from any inhabited land. I was far more isolated than a shipwreck survivor on a raft in the middle of the ocean. You can imagine my surprise, then, when a strange little voice woke me at daybreak. It said:
paras.zh: 于是，第一天晚上，我就在沙地上睡着了，离任何有人居住的地方都有一千英里。我比一个遭遇海难、漂在大洋中央木筏上的人还要孤立无援。所以你们可以想象，天刚亮时，一个奇怪的小小声音把我叫醒，我有多么惊讶。那声音说：

paras.en: “Please... draw me a sheep!”
paras.zh: “请……给我画一只绵羊！”

paras.en: “What!”
“Draw me a sheep...”
paras.zh: “给我画一只绵羊……”

paras.en: I jumped to my feet as though I had been struck by lightning. I gave my eyes a good rub. I took a good look. And I saw a quite extraordinary little fellow watching me solemnly. Here is the best portrait I later managed to draw of him. But my drawing, of course, is far less charming than its model. It is not my fault. Grown-ups had discouraged me in my career as a painter at the age of six, and I had learnt to draw nothing except closed boa constrictors and open boa constrictors.
paras.zh: 我一下子跳了起来，好像被雷劈中了一样。我使劲揉了揉眼睛。我仔细看了看。我看见一个很不寻常的小人儿，正神情严肃地打量着我。这就是后来我能给他画出的最好的一幅肖像。当然，我的画远没有他本人那么可爱。这可不能怪我。六岁时，大人们就让我对当画家这件事灰了心，除了合着的蟒蛇和剖开的蟒蛇，我什么也没学会画。

paras.en: So I stared at this apparition, my eyes round with astonishment. Do not forget that I was a thousand miles from any inhabited region. Yet my little fellow seemed neither lost, nor dead tired, nor dying of hunger, nor dying of thirst, nor scared to death. He looked nothing at all like a child lost in the middle of the desert, a thousand miles from any inhabited region. When I finally managed to speak, I said to him:
paras.zh: 我惊讶得瞪圆了眼睛，望着这个突然出现的小人儿。别忘了，我当时离任何有人居住的地方都有一千英里。可眼前这个小人儿，看起来既没有迷路，也没有累得要死，没有饿得要死，没有渴得要死，更没有吓得要死。他一点也不像一个迷失在沙漠中央、离任何有人居住的地方都有一千英里的孩子。等我终于说得出话来，我问他：

paras.en: “But what are you doing here?”
paras.zh: “可是，你在这里做什么？”

paras.en: And then he repeated to me, very softly, as though it were something very serious:
paras.zh: 他便又轻轻地对我说了一遍，仿佛这是一件十分严肃的事：

paras.en: “Please... draw me a sheep...”
paras.zh: “请……给我画一只绵羊……”

paras.en: When a mystery is too overwhelming, you do not dare disobey. Absurd as it seemed to me, a thousand miles from anywhere people lived and in danger of dying, I took a sheet of paper and a fountain pen from my pocket. But then I remembered that I had mostly studied geography, history, arithmetic and grammar, and I told the little fellow (a little crossly) that I did not know how to draw. He replied:
paras.zh: 当神秘的事情太让人震撼时，人就不敢不听从了。我离所有有人居住的地方都有一千英里，又有丧命的危险，这件事在我看来再荒唐，我还是从口袋里拿出了一张纸和一支钢笔。可是这时我想起，我主要学过的是地理、历史、算术和语法，于是我告诉小家伙（带着一点不高兴），我不会画画。他回答我：

paras.en: “That doesn’t matter. Draw me a sheep.”
paras.zh: “没关系。给我画一只绵羊。”

paras.en: Since I had never drawn a sheep, I drew one of the only two drawings I could manage all over again for him. The one of the closed boa constrictor. And I was astonished to hear the little fellow reply:
paras.zh: 因为我从来没画过绵羊，就把我仅会画的两幅画中的一幅，重新画给他看。就是蟒蛇闭着的那幅。听到小家伙的回答，我惊呆了：

paras.en: “No! No! I don’t want an elephant inside a boa constrictor. A boa constrictor is very dangerous, and an elephant takes up so much room. Where I live, it’s very small. I need a sheep. Draw me a sheep.”
paras.zh: “不！不！我不要蟒蛇肚子里的一头大象。蟒蛇很危险，大象又太占地方。我住的地方小得很。我需要一只绵羊。给我画一只绵羊。”

paras.en: So I drew.
paras.zh: 于是我画了起来。

paras.en: He looked carefully, then:
paras.zh: 他仔细看了看，然后说：

paras.en: “No! That one is already very ill. Draw another.”
paras.zh: “不！这一只已经病得很重了。再画一只。”

paras.en: I drew:
paras.zh: 我画了：

paras.en: My friend gave a kind, forgiving smile:
paras.zh: 我的朋友温和地笑了，带着宽容：

paras.en: “You can see… that’s not a sheep, it’s a ram. It has horns…”
paras.zh: “你看嘛……这不是绵羊，是公绵羊。它长着角……”

paras.en: So I drew it yet again. But this drawing was rejected too, like the ones before it:
paras.zh: 于是我又重新画了一次。可这幅画也和前面几幅一样，被拒绝了：

paras.en: “That one is too old. I want a sheep that will live a long time.”
paras.zh: “这只太老了。我要一只能活很久的绵羊。”

paras.en: Then, out of patience and eager to start taking my engine apart, I scribbled this drawing.
paras.zh: 这时，我已经没了耐心，又急着开始拆卸我的发动机，就草草画了这幅画。

paras.en: And I said abruptly:
paras.zh: 接着我甩出一句：

paras.en: “That’s the crate. The sheep you want is inside.”
paras.zh: “这是箱子。你要的绵羊就在里面。”

paras.en: But I was very surprised to see my young judge’s face light up:
paras.zh: 可看到我这位小裁判的脸亮了起来，我真是吃了一惊：

paras.en: “That’s just how I wanted it! Do you think this sheep will need a lot of grass?”
paras.zh: “我想要的就是这样的！你觉得这只绵羊需要很多草吗？”

paras.en: “Why?”
paras.zh: “为什么？”

paras.en: “Because where I live is very small…”
paras.zh: “因为我住的地方很小很小……”

paras.en: “There’s sure to be enough. I’ve given you a very small sheep.”
paras.zh: “肯定够的。我给你的是一只很小很小的绵羊。”

paras.en: He bent his head towards the drawing:
paras.zh: 他朝着画低下头：

paras.en: “Not all that small... Look! He's fallen asleep...”
paras.zh: “也没那么小……咦！它睡着了……”

paras.en: And that was how I came to know the little prince.
paras.zh: 就这样，我认识了小王子。
